subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A typical multiple-choice or fill-in-the-blank exam question requires a student to narrow down all possible ideas to arrive at one single correct answer. According to Guilford, this type of thinking is called:
explanation: Convergent thinking narrows multiple pieces of information down to a single correct answer — the pattern rewarded by conventional exams — in contrast to divergent thinking, which generates many possible original solutions and is the hallmark of creativity.
